picks.rationale: Start it now and wait on nothing. An adjusted PFS HR of 0.41 with median OS 33 vs 24 months (aHR 0.65) in her exact first-line population is the biggest effect size anywhere in this dossier, and for once the aggressive option and the best-evidenced option are the same regimen. The toxicity is heavy (G3-4 neutropenia 80%, febrile neutropenia 28%), but she is 39 and I will trade a hard six months of induction for a shot at the 33-month arm. The off-label first-line authorization is paperwork, not a reason to hesitate, and the molecular workup I want runs in parallel at zero cost in treatment days.
primary_concerns: Febrile neutropenia in 28%: growth-factor support should be planned before cycle 1, and her altitude-shifted hemoglobin baseline will confound anemia and dose-modification calls
The maintenance phase is empirical, with no preclinical support of any kind; its contribution cannot be separated from induction outside the trial design
Off-label at this line: a payer denial is the one thing that could actually delay induction, so the authorization file should go in before the first fill
Baseline LVEF and a documented ECOG are still missing and the trial required both

picks.intervention_label: Olaparib + temozolomide (queued for first progression, HRD workup during induction)
picks.rationale: This is where the upside hides in her untested genome. If the tumor lands in the HRD subset, the NCI 10250 numbers (ORR 27%, mPFS 6.9 months, and an 11.2 vs 5.4 month split by RAD51 foci) plus the BRCA2-deleted PDX work make this the strongest second-line bet in the disease, oral and potentially durable. Twenty-two patients, single-arm, I know. Order the HRR panel and HRD-relevant tissue work during induction so the answer is already sitting in the chart the day LMS-04 stops working.
primary_concerns: n=22 single-arm; the RAD51-foci split is exploratory and could evaporate in the randomized successor
Hematologic toxicity (G3-4 neutropenia 75% per abstract) stacks badly on marrow that just absorbed LMS-04 induction
Both trials are closed to accrual, so access is an off-label combination authorization; no RAD51 assay has a CLIA catalogue provider
If HRD testing comes back proficient, the expected benefit drops toward the 5.4-month arm and this pick loses most of its case

picks.intervention_label: REC-617 (CDK7 inhibitor) after RB1-null IHC, second line (NCT07633756)
picks.rationale: I am taking the thinnest branch in the case on purpose, because the stain that opens it costs one slide and RB1 loss is near-universal in this histology. If the IHC reads null, she has a first-in-class CDK7 inhibitor recruiting at MD Anderson for exactly her genotype after one prior line, and the RB1-null replication-stress mechanism from small-cell lung cancer is a real one even though nobody has run it in leiomyosarcoma. Zero LMS data, phase 1b, safety primary endpoint; that is the honest price of being early. She can pay it at second line rather than instead of LMS-04, which is the only way I would offer it.
primary_concerns: No CDK7 data of any kind in leiomyosarcoma; the mechanistic case is borrowed from RB1-null SCLC and YKL-5-124 is not REC-617
Phase 1b dose escalation means she could be treated at a subtherapeutic dose
Requires a biopsy-amenable lesion and RECIST-measurable disease, both uncertain against her infiltrative pulmonary pattern
Single site (Houston) and her travel tolerance was never actually stated

picks.intervention_label: MGC026 (B7-H3 ADC), phase 1 with named sarcoma cohort (NCT06242470)
picks.rationale: B7-H3 is the surface target most likely to actually be there: 97% of soft-tissue sarcomas stain positive and 69% at high level, and the duocarmycin bystander data say heterogeneous expression is survivable for this drug class. MGC026 is recruiting US sites with sarcoma on the named list and no expression gate, so a single stain on the 2024 archival block tells us whether the referral is worth booking. The class carries a corpse: MacroGenics' previous B7-H3 ADC was terminated after safety findings, and there is no LMS efficacy signal yet for the successor. I still want the stain run during induction, because a strong positive would make this the most reachable experimental door at second or third line.
primary_concerns: Predecessor vobramitamab duocarmazine was halted on safety in prostate cancer; payload liability is the live question for the whole class
Phase 1 dose escalation with no LMS response data at all
Positivity is not dependency: the CAR-T antigen-density work says low expressors gain little, so the 69% high-level stratum is the number that matters, not the 97%

picks.intervention_label: [225Ac]RTX-2358 FAP-targeted alpha radioligand (NCT07156565), FAPi PET as gate
picks.rationale: An alpha emitter whose eligibility question is answered by a PET scan she can get after one prior regimen, in a tumor family near the top of the FAP expression range with the antigen on the malignant cells themselves rather than only stroma. Radioligand crossfire does not care about the antigen heterogeneity that undermines ADC and cell-therapy cutoffs, and 177Lu-FAP-2286 already produced regressions in sarcoma PDX. The marrow-stroma FAP toxicity from the CAR-T mouse work is what I watch, though a renally cleared peptide is a very different exposure from a persisting engineered T cell. Screen her the month LMS-04 progresses; the scan itself settles whether the target exists.
primary_concerns: FAP sits on bone marrow stromal cells and FAP CAR-T caused lethal marrow toxicity in mice; dosimetry, not IHC, will decide whether that transfers
Phase 1 dose escalation with no human sarcoma efficacy for this specific agent
FAP PET uptake is unmeasured and ECOG 0-1 is required against an ECOG that was assumed at intake, never documented

notes: The real risktaker move in this case is diagnostic, and I want that on the record even though it is not a rankable intervention: one comprehensive DNA+RNA panel, one IHC block (RB1, B7-H3, HER2, PD-L1, ATRX) and an HLA typing blood draw, all run during induction, open or close nearly every experimental door in this dossier at once, including the TCR-T class I did not rank because both of its gates are unmeasured. Nothing recruiting closes when LMS-04 starts, so none of my picks 2-5 costs her anything today; they cost tissue and scheduling. I also want the 2024 operative report pulled, since morcellation status roughly triples abdominopelvic recurrence risk and changes surveillance imaging. No toxicity vetoes exist in preferences.json, but every preference value is an assumed default, so the aggressive framing I am arguing from (maximal disease control in a 39-year-old) is itself an inference the team must confirm with her.

picks.rationale: This is the rare case where the safety argument and the efficacy argument land on the same regimen: randomized phase 3 in her histology, mPFS 12.2 vs 6.2 months (HR 0.41, 95% CI 0.29-0.58), and at 55 months median follow-up an OS of 33 vs 24 months (HR 0.65, 95% CI 0.44-0.95). The price is printed on the trial itself, G3-4 neutropenia 80%, thrombocytopenia 47%, febrile neutropenia 28%, and I want it priced into the cycle 1 orders as primary G-CSF prophylaxis rather than discovered at cycle 2. My endorsement is conditional on a baseline battery that does not exist yet, because not one organ-function value is on file days before an anthracycline: echocardiogram with LVEF, hepatic and renal panels with CK, CBC with reticulocytes and ferritin, PFTs with DLCO and oximetry done at her 8,500 ft residence, and an examined ECOG. These toxicities are cytopenias and transaminitis with forty years of management algorithms behind them, which is why I can rank a regimen this rough first.
primary_concerns: No baseline organ function of any kind is documented: no LVEF, no hepatic or renal panel, no CBC, no PFTs. Every gating test for this regimen is missing with induction imminent.
Febrile neutropenia ran 28% vs 9% in LMS-04; primary G-CSF prophylaxis belongs in the cycle 1 orders.

She is 39. Cumulative doxorubicin dose planning and a dexrazoxane conversation belong before cycle 1, not at cycle 6; her survivorship horizon for anthracycline cardiomyopathy runs decades past this regimen.

Altitude changes three baselines at once: polycythaemia at 8,500 ft will mask chemotherapy anaemia, sea-level oximetry thresholds do not apply to her, and her presenting dyspnea cannot be split between disease and altitude without a measured local baseline.

Maintenance-phase trabectedin safety detail from LMS-04 is not publicly retrievable, so monitoring defaults to the SAR-3007 single-agent dossier (G>=3 ALT elevation 25%, rhabdomyolysis 1.2%, treatment-related deaths 2.1%); CK and LFTs stay on the recurring schedule through maintenance.
First-line use sits outside the trabectedin label, which requires prior anthracycline; the prior authorization should be filed as off-label from day one with the LMS-04 papers attached.

picks.rationale: This is the fallback I want pre-positioned, not a rival: GeDDiS tested gem-doce head-to-head against doxorubicin in an LMS-enriched population and found no superiority (24-week PFS 46.4% vs 46.3%, HR 1.28), which settles the first-line question in favor of the anthracycline backbone. Its role here is conditional, for the scenario where the echocardiogram or her pulmonary reserve at altitude disqualifies full-dose doxorubicin. The toxicity trade is familiar, with less febrile neutropenia than doxorubicin in GeDDiS (12% vs 20%) and both drugs generic after decades of use. The uLMS-specific first-line estimate is modest and worth stating plainly: ORR 35.8%, mPFS 4.4 months in GOG 087L.
primary_concerns: Both components carry pneumonitis risk and GOG 087L logged one grade 4 pulmonary event in 42 patients; against bilateral infiltrative lung disease read at 8,500 ft, any new hypoxia will be hard to attribute.

mPFS 4.4 months first line is roughly a third of what LMS-04 delivered, so falling back here has a real efficacy cost; the baseline testing that decides between the two regimens should be treated as urgent.

picks.rationale: I want pazopanib named now so the later-line conversation starts from an approved, well-characterized floor. PALETTE was placebo-controlled (PFS HR 0.31, 95% CI 0.24-0.40; mPFS 4.6 vs 1.6 months), the drug has been marketed since 2012, and its hypertension and liver toxicity come with standing monitoring algorithms rather than open questions. The uterine-sarcoma pooled analysis put all five partial responses in LMS, with mPFS 3.0 months in a heavily pretreated group. She becomes label-eligible the day LMS-04 stops working, with no travel and no biomarker gate.
primary_concerns: No OS benefit in PALETTE (HR 0.86, p=0.25); this buys progression-free time and that should be said plainly when the moment comes.
Boxed hepatotoxicity warning; the label's LFT schedule is routine work but it has to actually happen, alongside a blood pressure plan at initiation.
mPFS 3.0 months in the uterine subset tempers expectations relative to the all-comers PALETTE figure.

picks.rationale: I will carry one non-cytotoxic branch, olaparib plus temozolomide, and hold it behind two gates: her still-unmeasured HRR/HRD status and the exhaustion of better-characterized options. The signal is real but small, ORR 27% and mPFS 6.9 months in 22 patients, and the RAD51-deficient split (11.2 vs 5.4 months) is exploratory. What keeps it on my list is that both drugs have been marketed for years and the trial managed heavy hematologic toxicity with dose reductions rather than discontinuations (3/22 stopped for toxicity, no treatment-related deaths). Until the randomized successor reads out, this stays a biomarker-anchored off-label appeal.
primary_concerns: Single-arm, n=22, and the confirmatory randomized trial (NCT05432791) is closed to new accrual, so the evidence will not improve on any near-term clock.
G3/4 neutropenia around 75% stacked after LMS-04's 80% assumes marrow recovery that should be shown on a CBC before this is ever prescribed.
The somatic HRR and germline panels off the archival block gate this branch entirely; send them now, because an unmeasured HRD status makes the payer case and the clinical case equally weak.

picks.rationale: On safety grounds SBRT is easy to defend: zero grade 3 or higher events across both sarcoma series, local control 90% (95% CI 84-96) at 24 months in the larger one, and the technique is routine at any stereotactic-capable center. Everything else about it is conditional. The published series treated up to about four discrete lesions in selected patients, and her current pattern is bilateral and infiltrative, so candidacy exists only if induction converts the anatomy. The PFTs with DLCO that the chemotherapy baseline already requires are the same tests that will bound how much lung can be treated, so that work pays twice.
primary_concerns: Retrospective, selection-heavy series; local control is not survival, and the 5-year OS figures describe patients screened for exactly the anatomy she does not currently have.
Lung dose constraints must be set against pulmonary reserve measured at her residence altitude; sea-level norms will overcall her reserve.

notes: Two things on the record beyond the picks. Nothing in preferences.json was stated by the patient: the 0.7 efficacy-toxicity weight, the empty veto list, and the trials preference are intake defaults, and the ECOG of 1 was assumed, so none of my rankings treat those values as her position. No veto this round because there is no stated veto to enforce; my rank-1 endorsement is instead conditional on the pre-induction battery (LVEF, hepatic and renal panels with CK, CBC with reticulocytes and ferritin, PFTs with DLCO and oximetry at 8,500 ft, examined ECOG) being completed and passed, and I will treat an unmet condition as veto-grade in round 2 if induction is scheduled over it. Separately, two cheap documents change the safety picture: the September 2024 operative report settles the morcellation question and with it the surveillance-imaging plan, and a locally measured altitude baseline is the only thing that will make anaemia and pneumonitis calls readable on treatment. The dexrazoxane and cumulative-dose conversation belongs at treatment start; at 39 her anthracycline exposure is a lifetime ledger, not a per-regimen one.

picks.intervention_label: Doxorubicin + trabectedin induction, then trabectedin maintenance (LMS-04)
picks.rationale: Randomized phase 3, n=150, pre-specified primary PFS endpoint read by blinded independent central review: 12.2 vs 6.2 months, adjusted HR 0.41 (0.29-0.58), p<0.0001, and the 55-month analysis held on survival at 33 vs 24 months, adjusted HR 0.65 (0.44-0.95). This is the only RCT-grade, indication-matched result in the dossier, and it survives my scrutiny. Two things I will not let pass unstated: uterine primaries were 67 of 150, a stratified subgroup rather than a separately powered population, and the trabectedin maintenance phase was never tested against stopping, so how much of the 12.2 months it contributes is unmeasured. One trial, one cooperative group, no replication yet; SaLuDo (NCT06088290) is the nearest confirmatory read and has not reported.
primary_concerns: RoB 2, outcome measurement: the trial is open label. Blinded central review on the PFS primary handles most of the detection-bias worry and OS is not exposed to it, so this is the one open-label design I am comfortable with.
Indirectness. Uterine LMS was 67/150. Stratified randomisation is not power, and no uterine-specific effect estimate with its own confidence interval is printed in the abstract.

Maintenance is an untested component of a tested regimen. Nothing in this dossier randomises trabectedin continuation against stopping, and the preclinical basis for the pairing itself was additive at best (combination indices just under 1, pmid:12783202). MELODY (NCT06981637) asks the analogous maintenance question with pegylated liposomal doxorubicin, and it is in Taiwan.
Imprecision. 107 deaths among 150 patients and an OS upper bound of 0.95. The survival claim is real but it is not robust to one contradicting trial.

Selective reporting on the maintenance phase specifically: NCT02997358 has no posted results and the 2024 survival report gives no per-term adverse-event rates, so the toxicity of the part she may stay on longest is the part with the thinnest published detail.
Eligibility drift against her own file. The trial required ECOG 0-1 and cardiac clearance; her ECOG 1 is an intake assumption and no LVEF exists.

picks.rationale: GeDDiS is the only randomised first-line head-to-head carrying a real uLMS fraction, and it did not favour gemcitabine-docetaxel: 24-week PFS rate 46.4% vs 46.3%, HR 1.28 (0.99-1.65), p=0.06 pointing toward doxorubicin. uLMS was 71 of 257 with interaction p=0.38, so no uLMS-specific effect estimate exists in that trial and nobody should quote one as if it did. The uLMS numbers come from single-arm work instead, where the much-cited 53% ORR (n=34, one centre, 16 of 34 anthracycline-pretreated) fell to 35.8% (90% CI 23.5-49.6) with mPFS 4.4 months once a cooperative group ran it first line in n=42. I still rank it second, because if baseline LVEF or DLCO rules out doxorubicin this is the best-documented non-anthracycline first line she has.
primary_concerns: The 53% ORR is the textbook single-centre estimate that halved on cooperative-group replication. Quote 35.8% or quote both, never the 2002 number alone.
ROBINS-I moderate on both uLMS rows: single arm, no comparator, unblinded response assessment, mixed lines in the 2002 series.

One grade 4 pulmonary event in 42 patients (2.4%), judged possibly related. Both drugs carry pneumonitis risk, and she has bilateral infiltrative lung disease read against an 8,500 ft oximetry baseline that nobody has quantified.
The interaction p=0.38 is a null-for-heterogeneity test on 257 patients, which is weak reassurance rather than evidence that the uterine subset behaves like the whole.

picks.rationale: Credit where it is due: NCI 10250 pre-specified a one-stage binomial bar of 5 or more responses in 22 patients and hit it, with best ORR within 6 months of 23% and mPFS 6.9 months (95% CI 5.4-NE). Everything past that is hypothesis-grade. n=22, single arm, no comparator, an erratum on the record, and the RAD51-foci split everyone quotes (11.2 vs 5.4 months, p=0.05) comes from 9 of 18 evaluable patients in an exploratory analysis sitting exactly on the alpha boundary with no multiplicity control. The practical problem is worse than the statistical one: the RAD51 assay has no CLIA provider anywhere, so the stratifier that produced the signal cannot be measured on her, and the measurable substitute is HRR sequencing, where confirmed HRD ran 5 of 58 uLMS and in every confirmed case was a homozygous BRCA2 deletion.
primary_concerns: Internal reporting inconsistency worth naming: grade 3-4 neutropenia is 75% in the abstract and 13/22 (59%) for the neutropenia term in full-text Table 2. When the two published figures for the same toxicity disagree by 16 points in a 22-patient trial, I read the safety claim cautiously.

Both trials are active-not-recruiting (NCT03880019, NCT05432791), so this is off-label prescribing on single-arm data, not trial access. The randomised successor also requires 2 or more prior lines including an anthracycline and excludes prior temozolomide or dacarbazine, which constrains what can be given in between.
The biomarker branch that gates this is the one that cannot be run as published. Ordering HRR/BRCA2 sequencing is right; presenting it as the same test that generated the 11.2-month figure is not.
Response rate without a control arm in a disease where dacarbazine produced 9% in a randomised setting. 23% is a signal, not an effect estimate.

picks.intervention_label: Retrieval of the September 2024 operative report (morcellation question)
picks.rationale: Two independent retrospective cohorts point the same way: n=58 with multivariate-adjusted HR 3.18 (1.5-6.8) for recurrence and mRFS 10.8 vs 39.6 months, and an independent Korean series of 56 with OR 3.11 (1.07-9.06) for worse survival and abdominopelvic dissemination in 44% vs 12.9%. Replication across two centres in two health systems is more than most of this dossier can claim, even with ROBINS-I Serious on both rows. The obvious confounder runs toward the null here rather than away from it, since the morcellated tumours in the Korean series were the smaller ones. Pulling the operative report costs nothing and changes abdominopelvic surveillance imaging, which is a decision, not a history-taking detail.
primary_concerns: Both cohorts are retrospective with serious risk of bias, small (58 and 56), and neither adjusts for the era-dependent surgical practice that determined who got morcellated in the first place.
Effect sizes are imprecise. An OR whose lower bound is 1.07 is a direction, not a magnitude.
This changes surveillance and prognostic framing. It does not change what systemic therapy she gets, and it should not be sold to her as if it did.

picks.intervention_label: Lung-directed local therapy (metastasectomy or SBRT), conditional on induction response
picks.rationale: Everything supporting lung-directed local therapy here is retrospective and selected for operability: a 5,206-case registry (36% five-year survival after complete resection, 45% when the disease-free interval was 36 months or more), 31 LMS patients at one hospital with median OS 70 months, and SBRT series of 44 and 28 patients, ROBINS-I Serious across all four. Those figures describe patients whose disease was discrete and resectable. Hers is bilateral and infiltrative, which is the pattern these series screen out, so no expected outcome can honestly be attached to this option today. It belongs on the list as a question to re-ask if induction converts the anatomy, and it should be written down that way rather than as a survival number.
primary_concerns: Selection bias is the whole result. The registry's disease-free-interval and lesion-count strata are prognostic markers of who was chosen for surgery, and reading them as treatment effects inflates the benefit.
Local control is not survival. Baumann reports 90% control at 24 months (84-96) alongside 46% survival at 24 months (38-55) in the same 44 patients.
No randomised comparison of metastasectomy against continued systemic therapy exists anywhere in this dossier, and none is proposed.
Candidacy rests on pulmonary reserve that has never been measured. PFTs and DLCO are undone and the 8,500 ft baseline shifts every threshold used to judge them.
The two registered trials at this decision point are a phase 1/2 feasibility study (NCT03965234) and a China-only phase 2 (NCT06074692). Neither produces an efficacy estimate she could rely on.

notes:
PMID trap checked, and upstream handled it correctly. 36174625 is logged as considered_excluded with the right reason (a letter about LMS-04, not the trial), the PFS row cites 35835135 and the survival row cites 39231341. No drift found in the trials or evidence files.

On the 23-month interval: the EORTC pooled analysis of 2,185 first-line anthracycline patients does list a long time lapse since initial diagnosis as independently favourable (p=0.0004), alongside good performance status, absence of liver metastases, low grade and young age. But that variable was measured in patients whose sarcoma had been diagnosed and then followed. Hers encodes a pathology error plus whatever biology filled the gap, which is not the same exposure. The direction is plausible and she matches the model's population in age and line of therapy, so I would let the reading stand as reassurance; I would not carry the p-value into a prognosis conversation as though it had been measured on her variable.

Branches I would not fund at this board. REC-617 has no leiomyosarcoma data of any kind, and the rationale behind it is RB1/TP53-null small-cell lung cancer with a different compound (pmid:31883968); because RB1 loss is near-universal in LMS, the RB stain is more likely to route her into that empty arm than into the abemaciclib one, which is a strange way to design a decision. The abemaciclib + gemcitabine trial (NCT06498648) carries a mechanistic contradiction: CDK4/6 inhibition protected RB-proficient cells from concurrent genotoxic therapy with viable populations recurring afterwards (pmid:22751436), while the sequential-priming result that does work in Rb-positive LMS xenografts (pmid:28619757) is not the schedule the trial uses. ATR inhibition for ALT failed replication twice against the original claim (pmid:27602331 and pmid:33344901 against pmid:25593184), and ATRX loss or ALT prevalence in uLMS (pmid:26891131) is prevalence, not dependency. B7-H3 repeats that error at 97% positivity; the number that would matter is the 69.2% high-expression stratum, since efficacy fell away below an antigen-density threshold (pmid:30655315), and no LMS model exists for any B7-H3 agent in this dossier. Eribulin in LMS is null on every endpoint reported (OS HR 0.93, 0.71-1.2, p=0.57; PFS HR 1.07, 0.84-1.38), and pazopanib's uLMS evidence is a retrospective pooling of 44 heavily pretreated patients inside two prospective trials (ORR 11%, 3.8-24.6; mPFS 3.0 months). Neither belongs above the cytotoxic backbone, and letrozole is foreclosed at ER <1% / PR <1% since the only durable benefit in that 27-patient study occurred in tumours staining in more than 90% of cells.

picks.rationale: This is the plan her sarcoma oncologist already made, and it carries the best evidence in the file: mPFS 12.2 vs 6.2 months (adjusted HR 0.41) and final OS 33 vs 24 months (HR 0.65) in chemo-naive LMS. I back it, but the record should show that nobody has asked her whether she accepts 80% G3-4 neutropenia and 28% febrile neutropenia for that gain; the 0.7 efficacy weight that would settle the question is an intake default, not her answer. First-line use also sits outside the trabectedin label, which requires prior anthracycline, so the authorization request should go in now, citing LMS-04, rather than surfacing as a denial at the pharmacy. Every gating test (LVEF, altitude-read PFTs and oximetry, documented ECOG, RECIST baseline imaging) runs in parallel without delaying cycle 1.
primary_concerns: Consent gap: the 80% G3-4 neutropenia / 28% febrile neutropenia trade has never been put to her, and efficacy_toxicity_weight 0.7 is an assumed default
Off-label first line: the current Yondelis label requires prior anthracycline, so prior authorization is a real fight to start now
No measured baselines exist: LVEF, PFTs, labs, and ECOG are all assumptions or absences before an anthracycline at 8,500 ft

picks.intervention_label: Olaparib + temozolomide (post-LMS-04 branch, opened by NGS now)
picks.rationale: The strongest non-cytotoxic signal in uLMS: ORR 27% and mPFS 6.9 months, with responses lasting around a year. It is also oral, which would matter if she turns out to care about time in the infusion chair; nobody knows, because nobody asked. The branch only exists if the HRD-relevant NGS goes in now: results take 2-3 weeks, both dedicated trials are closed to accrual, and the interim route is off-label prescribing with payer friction. At n=22 and single-arm this stays a next-line branch rather than a challenger to LMS-04.
primary_concerns: n=22, single-arm; the 27% ORR is hypothesis-grade until NCT05432791 reads out
Both dedicated uLMS trials closed to accrual, so the interim route is an off-label prescription her insurer can push back on
Gated on HRD/NGS testing that has not been ordered yet
G3-4 neutropenia up to 75% lands on a marrow already hit by LMS-04

picks.intervention_label: Gemcitabine + docetaxel (first-line fallback if cardiopulmonary screening fails)
picks.rationale: Her fallback if the cardiopulmonary numbers come back bad, and with no LVEF, no PFTs, and an oximetry baseline shifted by 8,500 ft of altitude, a failed screen is a live possibility. The first-line uLMS data are modest but real: ORR 35.8%, mPFS 4.4 months in GOG 087L. GeDDiS showed no edge over doxorubicin, so a fit patient should still get LMS-04. I rank it so the plan survives a bad echo without a scramble.
primary_concerns: Cross-trial PFS gap vs LMS-04 (4.4 vs 12.2 months) makes this second choice for a fit patient
Gemcitabine and docetaxel both carry pneumonitis risk against bilateral infiltrative lung disease; one G4 pulmonary event in 42 patients in GOG 087L
Only becomes first choice if the unmeasured cardiopulmonary baseline fails

picks.rationale: If she wants a trial, this is the only recruiting first-line study in the dossier that takes systemic-treatment-naive LMS, and since only prior gemcitabine is barred, the door stays open after LMS-04 too. But prefers_trials: true is an intake default; her actual appetite for a single-site study in Houston, and the travel that means from a home at 8,500 ft, is something no one has asked her. Phase 1/2 with no LMS efficacy readout yet. I list it so someone asks her, because the evidence on its own does not compete with LMS-04.
primary_concerns: prefers_trials is an assumed default; trial appetite and travel tolerance were never stated
Single site (Houston); travel burden from an 8,500 ft residence unquantified
Phase 1/2, no LMS efficacy data yet

picks.intervention_label: Pulmonary metastasectomy (or SBRT) as post-induction consolidation
picks.rationale: The closest thing to a stated goal anywhere in this record is the plan she accepted: systemic control first, with local lung therapy kept on the table. Holding that consolidation branch in the ranking keeps faith with the one conversation she has actually had. The LMS metastasectomy series are surgeon-selected best cases (median OS 70 months in the Brigham LMS subset), and bilateral infiltrative disease is what those series screened out, so this only becomes real if induction converts her anatomy. Candidacy runs through the same altitude-anchored PFTs the anthracycline needs, so one test serves both decisions.
primary_concerns: Series are operability-selected; her current bilateral infiltrative anatomy would not qualify
Pulmonary reserve at altitude unmeasured, and the reserve math decides surgery and SBRT alike
Contingent on induction response; nobody needs to decide this today

notes: An odd round for this chair: preferences.json says outright that nothing in it came from her. So there is no preference filter to hold picks to, and the danger runs the other way, that the board treats intake defaults as her wishes. Anyone reasoning from 'she prefers trials' or 'efficacy weight 0.7' is quoting the system, not the patient. Four questions need asking before those defaults harden: whether she accepts 80% G3-4 neutropenia and 28% febrile neutropenia for a PFS HR of 0.41; whether she wants trials at all, and how far she will travel from a home at 8,500 ft; what ovarian function and the hormonal aftermath of chemotherapy mean to her at 39 (hysterectomy does not settle this, and no one has raised it); and how much off-label authorization fighting she will absorb, since her first-line regimen already needs some. None of the executable items wait on any of that: baseline LVEF, documented ECOG, RECIST baseline imaging, PFTs and oximetry read at altitude, the September 2024 operative report (morcellation roughly triples recurrence risk, adjusted HR 3.18), and the one NGS panel plus IHC bundle that opens or closes most targeted branches, all running in parallel with induction. One more thing, for the reporter: whoever reads the final document was told for 23 months that she did not have cancer. Write for that reader.

picks.rationale: The planned regimen is the only first-line option in this dossier with randomized survival data in her histology (mPFS 12.2 vs 6.2 months, aHR 0.41; final mOS 33 vs 24 months, aHR 0.65), and NCCN Uterine Neoplasms lists doxorubicin plus trabectedin among first-line systemic options for metastatic uLMS. I could confirm that carriage only through secondary sources this run because the guideline PDF sits behind a login, so I am not quoting an NCCN evidence category I have not seen. ESMO-EURACAN-GENTURIS 2021 (Ann Oncol 32:1348-65) predates LMS-04 and does not carry the combination, and the UK BSG 2025 guideline cites its PFS benefit while noting NICE has not adopted it, so cross-society convergence is incomplete but moving in one direction. Trabectedin's FDA label requires a prior anthracycline, which makes first-line use off-label; the payer request should lead with the NCCN listing and both trial publications rather than the label.
primary_concerns: LMS-04 required ECOG 0-1; her ECOG 1 is an intake assumption no clinician has documented.
Baseline LVEF, PFTs, and labs are all missing, so the trial's own cardiac and fitness screens have not been run, and her 8,500 ft baseline will confound anemia and oximetry calls on treatment.
G3-4 neutropenia 80% and febrile neutropenia 28% on the combination arm, heavier than any alternative first-line listing.
Off-label at this line under the trabectedin label's prior-anthracycline clause; the prior authorization should be filed as off-label from day one.

picks.rationale: This is the guideline-listed fallback if the pending echocardiogram or her pulmonary reserve rules out full-dose doxorubicin: long carried by NCCN for uLMS, listed in BSG 2025, and holding first-line uLMS data of its own (GOG 087L, ORR 35.8%, mPFS 4.4 months). GeDDiS settles the ordering, showing no superiority over doxorubicin in an LMS-enriched population (PFS HR 1.28), so it stays second choice for as long as the anthracycline door is open.
primary_concerns: GOG 087L logged a possibly treatment-related grade 4 pulmonary event; both drugs carry pneumonitis risk against bilateral infiltrative lung disease and an altitude-shifted oximetry baseline.
Whether this is needed at all depends on gating diagnostics that have not been done yet.

picks.intervention_label: Pulmonary metastasectomy (with SBRT as the non-surgical alternative) after systemic control
picks.rationale: BSG 2025 carries lung-directed local therapy in metastatic sarcoma, hanging the decision on disease-free interval, lesion number, and completeness of resection, with SABR named as an option where surgery does not fit; it cites the ESMO-EURACAN-GENTURIS guideline for the same criteria. That matches the consulting oncologist's stated plan: induction first, local therapy only if the disease converts to oligometastatic anatomy. The data behind the practice (5-year OS 36% after complete resection; median OS 70 months in one LMS surgical series) describes selected, operable patients, which she currently is not.
primary_concerns: Guideline carriage assumes discrete resectable lesions; bilateral infiltrative, possibly inflammatory disease is exactly what the surgical series screened out.
Surgical fitness will turn on PFTs and oximetry read against an 8,500 ft baseline, none of which exists yet.

The morcellation question from the 2024 hysterectomy is unresolved. BSG 2025 states laparoscopic morcellation is contraindicated in uterine sarcoma because it disseminates disease; if it happened, peritoneal staging needs settling before any lung-directed consolidation is planned.

picks.rationale: The on-label, guideline-listed later-line anchor: NCCN lists it for non-adipocytic STS and ESMO-EURACAN-GENTURIS 2021 includes it after chemotherapy, on PALETTE (PFS HR 0.31 vs placebo). She becomes label-eligible the day LMS-04 stops working, and any trial option at that point has to beat it. In the uterine subset the numbers are modest (ORR 11%, mPFS 3.0 months), which is worth saying before anyone frames it as more than a holding option.
primary_concerns: PALETTE required prior anthracycline, so this pick belongs to the next line, not now.
The uterine-sarcoma-specific evidence is a retrospective pooled subset of 44 patients.

picks.rationale: I could not verify NCCN carriage of this combination for uLMS this run, and the evidence is a 22-patient single-arm phase 2 (ORR 27%, mPFS 6.9 months), so from a guideline seat this is trial-preferred territory rather than a listed standard, and I am reporting it that way. The guideline-aligned move is the one already queued: somatic HRR panel plus germline testing now, and a watch on the randomized successor NCT05432791, currently closed to accrual, which is the study that would move this onto a pathway. ESMO's 2024 precision-medicine recommendations now name sarcoma among the tumors where NGS is recommended, so the profiling that gates this branch is itself guideline-backed.
primary_concerns: Both dedicated uLMS trials are closed to new accrual (verified against CT.gov this run); off-label access would rest on a payer appeal built around one phase 2.
HRD status is unmeasured, and the RAD51 functional assay that best separated outcomes has no orderable CLIA version.

notes: Guideline verification log for this run. (1) NCCN Uterine Neoplasms: the current release I could verify is v3.2025; PMID 40763788 resolves to 'NCCN Guidelines Insights: Uterine Neoplasms, Version 3.2025' (JNCCN 2025;23(8):284-291, doi 10.6004/jnccn.2025.0038), so the identifier the target_validator dropped is real. Its abstract scopes the Insights to FIGO 2023 staging and endometrial-cancer systemic updates, though, so it is not a content citation for the uLMS pathway; dropping it for that purpose was the right call. A later 2026 revision may exist behind the NCCN login, which I cannot see. (2) NCCN carriage of doxorubicin+trabectedin as a first-line metastatic uLMS option is confirmed through two independent secondary sources (Yang et al, Cells 2024, PMID 38994959, citing the NCCN Uterine Neoplasms guideline; plus the accessibility screener's compendium note). The NCCN evidence category is unverified; do not let downstream agents quote 2A on my account. (3) ESMO: the operative guideline is still the ESMO-EURACAN-GENTURIS STS CPG 2021 (Ann Oncol 32:1348-1365, PMID 34303806), published November 2021, before LMS-04; it cannot and does not carry the combination. Publisher blocks prevented full-text retrieval, so I quote no ESMO grades. No validated ESMO-MCBS scorecard for doxorubicin+trabectedin in this indication was confirmable, so I quote no MCBS score. (4) BSG 2025 (Br J Cancer, PMID 38734790, open access) is the one post-LMS-04 society guideline I could read in full: standard first-line remains single-agent doxorubicin (their grade I,A), the LMS-04 combination is acknowledged for PFS benefit but not NICE-supported, metastatic uterine LMS is treated like STS elsewhere (III,B), and endocrine options are limited to receptor-expressing, relatively indolent tumors, which her high-grade ER/PR <1% disease is not; the foreclosure holds. (5) Molecular profiling: ESMO Precision Medicine Working Group 2024 (PMID 38834388) now recommends tumor NGS in sarcoma and for tumor-agnostic alterations, which puts guideline weight behind the queued CGP; NCCN's biomarker-directed later-line options (pembrolizumab at TMB >=10 mut/Mb per the tumor-agnostic label) are what that panel would unlock. (6) Germline: the ERN GENTURIS Li-Fraumeni guideline (Frebourg et al, Eur J Hum Genet 2020, PMID 32457520) advises TP53 testing before treatment starts because genotoxic chemotherapy and radiotherapy raise second-primary risk in carriers. She is in her thirties with a high-grade sarcoma and doxorubicin is imminent; the germline draw should go out before cycle 1, not after. (7) Morcellation: BSG 2025 states laparoscopic morcellation is contraindicated in uterine sarcoma; retrieving the September 2024 operative report is the guideline-consistent staging step and costs a records request.
